The decree Execution caseNo.1 of 1996 arises out of Civil Petition for leave to appeal no.505 of 1993 and their Lordships of Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh dismissed the appeal on 16.6.1994 thereby affirmed the judgment and decree of the Hon'ble High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh on an Appeal from Appellate Decree No.929 of 1994, allowed the appeal by judgment and decree dated 12.8.1993 and thereby setting aside judgment and decree dated 30.11.1962 passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, Additional Court of Zilla Khulna passed in Title Appeal No.246 of 1960 reversing the judgment and decree dated 24.8;1960 in Title Suit No.143 of 1952, passed by the learned Munsiff, 2nd Court Bagerhat and the instant Decree Execution Case No.1 of 1995. 

 7. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas with Mr. Sadananda Rana the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the judgment debtor petitioners submit that the original title being No.143 of 1952 was filed for declaration and recovery of possession measuring an area of 55 Bighas of land and it was decreed but the decree holder opposite party nos:l-15 claimed excess land in the decreetal boundary after accretion upto the river totaling to land measuring 125 Bighas of land which is not the part of the decree and the court has gone beyond the original quantum of decreetal land in execution case which caused miscarriage of justice and further submits that he has no objection if an advocate Commissioner is appointed to locate the said 55 decimals of land as per decree of the trial court and it handed over to the Decree holder within Specified date. 

 9. Be that as it may the judgment and decree holder opposite parties are entitled to have the decree execution as obtained in title suit No.143 of 1952 and an execution proceeding seems to be obstructed on the ground that the excess land is going to be handed over. It seems that before filing of this present application the judgment debtor has also preferred similar application before this court which went up to Appellate Division and that was rejected. Therefore under this circumstances the application alleging that excess land is going to be delivered is just a decree to make delay in executing and delivering the possession of the decreetal land. Therefore the executing court must not make further delay in delivery of possession in respect of decreetal land by appointing an Advocate Commissioner after demarcating the boundary in respect of 55 Bighas of land as per schedule within one month from the date of receipt of this order. Accordingly this rule is discharged without any order as to costs.
